text: In 1994 the Air Force concluded that the debris found near Roswell in 1947 most likely came from Project Mogul, a classified program that flew trains of balloons carrying radar reflectors and acoustic sensors to determine the state of Soviet nuclear weapons research.
src_label: United States General Accounting Office (GAO) (July 1995); U.S. National Archives (National Archives and Records Administration)

quotes: In the July 1994 Report of Air Force Research Regarding the Roswell Incident, the Air Force did not dispute that something happened near Roswell, but reported that the most likely source of the wreckage was from a balloon-launched classified government project designed to determine the state of Soviet nuclear weapons research.

The Air Force report concluded that there was no dispute that something happened near Roswell in July 1947 and that all available official materials indicated the most likely source of the wreckage recovered was one of the project MOGUL balloon trains.

At the time of the Roswell crash, project MOGUL was a highly classified U.S. effort to determine the state of Soviet nuclear weapons research using balloons that carried radar reflectors and acoustic sensors.

sources.publisherFull: U.S. National Archives (National Archives and Records Administration)
quotes: On September 8, 1994, the Secretary of the Air Force, Sheila E. Widnall, announced that the United States Air Force had completed its study to locate records that relate to the alleged 1947 UFO incident near Roswell, New Mexico.

Information obtained through exhaustive records searches and interviews indicated that the materials recovered near Roswell were consistent with a balloon device of the type used in a then-classified project.
The Air Force research did not locate or develop any information that the "Roswell Incident" was a UFO event nor was there any indication of a "cover-up" by the Government.

In our search for records concerning the Roswell crash, we learned that some government records covering RAAF activities had been destroyed and others had not. text: At Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid’s direction, Congress appropriated $22 million in 2008 and 2010 for a Defense Intelligence Agency program known as AAWSAP, which ran from 2009 to 2012.

quotes: In the $600 billion annual Defense Department budgets, the $22 million spent on the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program was almost impossible to find.

The shadowy program — parts of it remain classified — began in 2007, and initially it was largely funded at the request of Harry Reid, the Nevada Democrat who was the Senate majority leader at the time and who has long had an interest in space phenomena.
Contracts obtained by The Times show a congressional appropriation of just under $22 million beginning in late 2008 through 2011.
The Defense Department has never before acknowledged the existence of the program, which it says it shut down in 2012.
